newsitem.title: SPAIN: Pryca, Continente rally on consumption data.
newsitem.headline: Pryca, Continente rally on consumption data.

text.p: Spanish hypermarkets Continente and Pryca sharply outpaced the stock market on Wednesday after first quarter gross domestic product (GDP) data showed a strong rise in private consumption, dealers said.

At 1245 GMT, Pryca was up 115 pesetas, 4.01 percent, to 2,980, while rival group Continente was up 150 pesetas, 4.99 percent, to 3,155 pesetas. The Ibex-35 blue chip index was up 0.98 percent to 6,863.72.

This morning the National Statistics Institute (INE) said GDP rose 2.9 percent year-on-year in the first quarter. Private consumption rose 2.8 percent on the year, and 1.0 percent from the previous quarter.
"Pryca and Continente are clearly favoured by the consumption recovery. But (the shares) may be a little expensive" said an analyst at an independent brokerage.
But a dealer at BBV Interactivos disagreed.
"The GDP data are pretty good, and they should provide the means for the hypermarkets to close the (performance) gap against the Ibex," said Alvaro Climent.
Dealers said there were foreign buyers in Continente, particularly from the UK, whereas Pryca buyers were more varied.
"We think these stocks are going to benefit not just from rising consumption here, but also in the rest of Europe," Climent added.
Interactivos' year-end target price for Pryca is 3,400 pesetas, while Continente is seen rising to 3,300 pesetas.
"Even though their (price-earnings) ratios are high, we consider that they have been penalised relative to the market," Climent added.
Both firms' earnings performance are thought likely to be better in 1998 than in 1997.

Banco Central Hispano's research department forecasts that GDP will rise 3.3 percent overall in 1997, versus 2.2 percent in 1996, with the private consumption component estimated to rise 3.3 percent itself.
